title: Practical GraphRAG: Making LLMs smarter with Knowledge Graphs — Michael, Jesus, and Stephen, Neo4j
talk_summary: Neo4j advocates GraphRAG: build a lexical graph of documents/chunks, extract entities and relationships with an LLM against a schema, enrich with graph algorithms, then retrieve by index-search entry points plus relationship traversal instead of pure vector similarity. They cite Microsoft/data.world accuracy and token-cost gains and show an agentic pattern where domain-specific Cypher-query tools are called in a loop.

takeaways.technique: Structured lexical graph over repo/docs instead of flat chunk RAG
takeaways.what_they_do: Represent documents as nodes with parent/predecessor/successor and kNN-similarity edges, then retrieve by following relationships from index-search entry points rather than returning isolated vector hits.
takeaways.numbers: Microsoft GraphRAG paper cited as better results and less token cost; data.world study cited 3x accuracy vs SQL RAG

takeaways.technique: Domain-specific retriever tools called in an agentic loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Each retriever is a tool wrapping one Cypher query with typed inputs and a description; an agent decomposes the question and calls tools in sequence or loop, drilling deeper on results.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you basically break down the user question into individual tasks and extract parameters and run these individual tools

takeaways.what_they_do: The demo surfaces which sources, chunks, and graph entities were passed to the LLM, making retrieval failures inspectable, and they mention running eval with RAGAS.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can actually really see from an explanability perspective these are the entities that have been retrieved

takeaways.technique: Schema-constrained entity extraction with existing ground truth
takeaways.what_they_do: Pass a graph schema plus already-known entities (products, clients) so the LLM recognizes and links rather than free-extracts, reducing drift and duplication.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can also pass this in as part of the prompt. So that the LLM doesn't do an extraction, but more an recognition

takeaways.what_they_do: Run graph algorithms (clustering, PageRank, community summarization) to produce cross-document topic summaries the LLM can consume instead of raw text.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you generate uh something like uh communities where an LLM can generate summaries uh across them
